mind_map.root_node: The Dairy Farm (Flexible Multiplication Strategies, Partial Products & Area Grids)

key_nodes: Zero Appending Rule: Multiply non-zero digits, then append total count of trailing zeroes
Examples: 45 x 10 = 450 (append 1 zero); 32 x 100 = 3,200 (append 2 zeroes); 7 x 1,000 = 7,000
Multiplication Identities: N x 0 = 0 (Zero property); N x 1 = N (Identity property)
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Appending zeroes when multiplying decimals without adjusting decimal point position.
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Zero Rule: Product = (A x B) with trailing zeroes appended equal to sum of zeroes in factors.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Calculating bulk dairy yields, crate box totals, and wholesale product billing.

key_nodes: Compensation Principle: Halving one factor and doubling the other keeps total product unchanged
Strategic Application: Convert difficult factors into easy multiples of 10 (e.g., 14 x 5 -> (14/2) x (5x2) = 7 x 10 = 70)
Nearest Multiple Adjustment: Multiplying by 9 or 19 via (N x 10) - N or (N x 20) - N
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Halving both factors or doubling both factors instead of applying inverse compensation.
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Halving & Doubling Identity: A x B = (A / 2) x (B x 2).
sub_branches.real_world_application: Rapid mental estimation of grocery prices and daily farm earnings.

key_nodes: Additive Decomposition: Decompose 2-digit factors into tens and ones (e.g., 23 x 12 = (20 + 3) x (10 + 2))
Grid Area Mapping: 2x2 grid representing 4 sub-rectangular areas (20x10=200, 20x2=40, 3x10=30, 3x2=6)
Distributive Law: a x (b + c) = (a x b) + (a x c)
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Forgetting to sum all four partial products in a 2x2 grid decomposition.
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Distributive Law: (A + B) x (C + D) = AC + AD + BC + BD.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Calculating compost pit surface areas, floor tiling needs, and auditorium seating capacity.

key_nodes: Column Alignment of Partial Products: Writing tens and ones partial products vertically
Carrying in Partial Multiplication: Managing place value overflow during column multiplication
Efficiency Comparison: Grid model provides visual conceptual understanding; column algorithm speeds computation
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Misaligning place values when writing partial product rows in vertical multiplication.
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Standard Multiplication Algorithm: Product = Sum of Ones Partial Row + Tens Partial Row.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Commercial farm accounting and calculating annual feed costs.

key_nodes: Daily Herd Production: Daily Volume = Number of Cows x Yield per Cow (litres)
Monthly Yield: Daily Herd Production x Days in Month (e.g., 30 days)
Gross Revenue: Total Revenue = Total Litres Sold x Price per Litre (₹)
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Calculating monthly revenue using 7 days instead of 30/31 days.
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Revenue = Herd Size x Daily Litres per Cow x Days x Rate per Litre.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Managing dairy cooperative finances, cattle feed budgeting, and milk packet distribution.

key_nodes: Organic Waste Conversion Ratios: Dung to organic fertilizer mass reduction
Compost Pit Surface Area: Calculating pit dimensions using grid area formulas
Environmental Cost Savings: Savings = Commercial Fertilizer Cost - Organic Compost Cost
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Assuming waste mass remains constant during organic decomposition.
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Net Cost Benefit = Fertilizer Purchase Saved - Pit Setup Cost.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Sustainable farming eco-audits and waste-to-wealth cooperative projects.
